--- Segmentation assertion (draft) ---
Redwood Inference implements a tenant-isolation architecture for Dedicated and Private deployments designed to minimize cross-customer exposure. For Dedicated deployments, each customer is provisioned in an isolated VPC (or equivalent tenant boundary) with dedicated compute pools, network ACLs, and private IP addressing. The data plane that serves inference requests is strongly isolated from other tenants by network segmentation and per-tenant runtime instances; encryption in transit and at rest is enforced using customer keys where requested.

For Private deployments (VPC-hosted or on-prem), the control plane can be optionally deployed in a customer-managed network or logically segmented control plane; control-plane telemetry and management operations are logically separated from customer data paths. Management-facing APIs and orchestration services communicate over authenticated channels that are restricted to specified management subnets and require mutual TLS.

Egress controls are enforced at the tenant boundary. Outbound traffic from customer workloads is routed through a managed egress gateway that enforces allowlists, DNS filtering, and TLS interception where required for threat inspection. All egress flows and control-plane operations are logged to immutable audit streams retained according to customer SLA and SOC 2 retention policy.

We map these boundaries to SIG/CAIQ controls as follows: network segmentation and per-tenant compute correspond to CAIQ/NW-01 and SIG Control Mappings for "network segmentation and tenancy isolation"; control-plane separation and authenticated management channels map to SIG controls on "management plane access"; egress enforcement maps to network egress controls and monitoring controls in CAIQ. Detailed control mappings are included in the attached spreadsheet.

--- end draft ---
